articles.title: Susana Rodríguez sigue imparable: ¡campeona del mundo por octava vez!
articles.standfirst: Aumenta, junto a Sara Pérez como guía, un palmarés de leyenda en un año en el que ha pasado por el quirófano. Nil Riudavets y Dani Molina, plata
articles.summary: Aumentando un palmarés de leyenda en un año en el que ha pasado por el quirófano. Nil Riudavets se colgó la plata en PTS4
articles.body: Con Susana Rodríguez se acaban los calificativos. No hay quien la frene, ni las rivales ni las lesiones. La triatleta gallega, junto a su guía Sara Pérez, ha conquistado su octavo título mundial (2012, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2022, 2024, 2025 y 2026) -el tercero consecutivo- y su decimotercera medalla mundial (3 platas y 2 oros). Además, lo ha hecho en Pontevedra, en casa, ante su familia y su gente. La pareja española ganó con autoridad, con otra exhibición y con tanta diferencia con sus rivales que unos metros antes de cruzar la meta, jaleadas por el speaker, saludaban al público. Después de cruzarla y fundirse en un abrazo eterno, se quedaron esperando a sus rivales junto a la meta para aplaudirlas. Un gesto que dice mucho de las campeonas. Rodríguez se sacó la espinita del Mundial de Pontevedra de 2023, en el que fue plata por una penalización, con una victoria implacable hoy (01:06:37). Sacó casi dos minutos a la italiana Francesca Tarantello (01:08:30) y más de tres (03:07) a la alemana Anja Renner. "Estoy muy contenta de conseguirlo aquí, de poder cambiar la historia y quedarme con este recuerdo para siempre, con el público, mi familia, mis amigos, mi entrenador y todos los niños y niñas que estaban animando", dijo a los periodistas. También recordó lo "duro" y "triste" que fue la penalización en Pontevedra en 2023, por eso ahora ve "cumplido el sueño" de triunfar en su casa. Junto a Pérez dominaron cada uno de los segmentos del triatlón en Pontevedra. Han formado un tándem de oro en la categoría PTVI para triatletas con discapacidad visual. La viguesa, bicampeona paralímpica (Tokio 2020 y París 2024), reapareció en junio para llevarse otro oro europeo en Tarragona apenas dos meses después de haber sido intervenida de la banda iliotibial derecha. Cuando en marzo decidió pasar por quirófano fue precisamente con el objetivo de poder estar en el Mundial. Pese a no estar al cien por cien recuperada, siguió sumando oros después en las Series Mundiales de Montreal y Hamburgo. De hecho, hace más de dos años que no se baja del primer cajón del podio internacional, concretamente desde el 1 de junio de 2024 en la Copa del Mundo de Vigo, en casa, en el que una caída con el tándem acabó con ella en el hospital. Después preparó el Mundial en el CAR de Sierra Nevada (Granada), antes de viajar a Pontevedra, donde la viguesa se instaló este mes para entrenar junto a Sara. Ya había avisado antes, a través de sus redes sociales, que la cita en Galicia iba a ser su última competición internacional en España mientras continúa su camino hacia Los Ángeles 2028, sus cuartos Juegos. Su despedida, o "fecha de jubilación" como ella misma dice, será ese mismo año en el Mundial de Nueva Zelanda, donde compitió precisamente en su primer campeonato del mundo. Le gustaría cerrar allí el círculo. Rodríguez ha jalonado su curriculum dorado pese a que en los últimos seis años ha tenido una carrera llena de obstáculos: en 2020 el diagnóstico de la cardiopatía y la pandemia; en 2022, el burnout (desgaste profesional); en el 2023, decisiones difíciles; en 2024, el accidente en Vigo con el tándem en competición a tres meses de los Juegos de París y en 2025, la arritmia y ablación. También subió al podio en Pontevedra Nil Riudavets, que se colgó la plata mundial en la categoría PTS4. El menorquín, bronce paralímpico en París 2024, cruzó la meta cuando el luminoso marcaba 01:00:07. Sólo 13 segundos después de que lo hubiese hecho el francés Alexis Hanquinquant, bicampeón paralímpico en Tokio 2020 y París 2024. El bronce también fue para el francés Pierre-Antoine Baele (01:00:17). Este mismo año, Riudavets fue bronce europeo. El tercer podio del día español llegó con Dani Molina, campeón paralímpico en París 2024, que sumó una plata en PTS3. Una medalla que demuestra la enorme calidad de este deportista, ya que este año apenas ha competido antes en tres eventos por problemas en la rodilla izquierda. El manchego, que tiró de experiencia, completó los 750 metros a nado, los 20 kilómetros en bici y los 5 kilómetros en carrera en un tiempo de 01:09:11, a 01:54 del británico Henry Urand, que se llevó el oro. Suma su duodécima medalla mundial (5 oros, 5 platas y 2 bronces). El griego Stylianos Malakopoulos fue bronce (01:10:13). En cuanto al resto de la participación española, Lionel Morales acabó quinto en PTS2 con un tiempo de 01:17:13, a 04:46 del ganador, el francés Jules Ribstein. En la prueba para las mujeres PTWC, que compiten con handbike en el tramo ciclista y con silla de ruedas en el de carrera, Eva Moral acabó sexta (01:16:41), a 06:28 de la australiana Lauren Parker (01:10:13), que se llevó el oro. Completaron el podio las estadounidenses Kendall Gretsch y Emelia Perry, plata y bronce respectivamente. En la categoría PTVI para triatletas masculinos con discapacidad visual, Héctor Catalá y su guía Diego Méntrida también acabaron sextos (01:02:08), a minuto y medio del británico Dave Ellis que se coronó campeón. La pareja había sido bronce este año en el Europeo. Los debutantes Diego Molina y con Alfonso Izquierdo como guía acabaron novenos, a 04:33 del oro, mientras que Abel Torreblanca y Ander Noain fueron décimos. Los cuatro son miembros del Equipo CaixaBank de Promesas Paralímpicas de Triatlón. Y en PTS5, María Fuertes acabó novena (01:17:38).

articles.title: Predictions for Ospreay, CM Punk and WWE Worlds Collide vs. AEW All Out's Battle for Chicago
articles.summary: WWE and AEW have had shows running at the same time before, but this is the first time both companies will be in the same city at the same time.
articles.body:
WWE and AEW have had shows running at the same time before, but this is the first time both companies will be in the same city at the same time.

Saturday night will see AEW hold its annual All Out PPV, and WWE will put on its Worlds Collide event featuring talents from NXT, WWE and AAA.

Not only will both promotions have a show on the same day, but it all takes place in CM Punk's hometown of Chicago, so he has been booked on Worlds Collide to help give the show a boost in star power.

Let's go through the card for each show and make some predictions.

La Catalina vs. Roxanna Perez (AAA Reina De Reinas Championship)

Axiom vs. Mini Vikingo vs. Je'Von Evans vs. EK Prosper

La Parka, Mr. Iguana, Adelicious and Mascarita Sagrada vs. The Vanity Project and Mini Abismo Negro

CM Punk, Rey Mysterio and El Grande Americano vs. Omos, Dominik Mysterio and JD McDonagh

Cage and Cope vs. FTR vs. Young Bucks (AEW Men's Tag Titles)

Brawling Birds vs. Divine Dominion (AEW Women's Tag Titles)

Swerve Strickland and New Level vs. Adam Page and Brodido (Trios Titles)

Thekla vs. Willow Nightingale (Women's World Title)

Darby Allin and Steven Borden vs. Kyle Fletcher and Kevin Knight

Kazuchika Okada vs. Tommaso Ciampa (International Title)

Andrade El Idolo vs. Pac (National Title)

Persephone vs. TBD (Open Challenge for the TBS Title)

Will Ospreay vs. Jon Moxley (World Heavyweight Championship)

The only title being defended on the Worlds Collide card is the Reina De Reinas Championship currently held by La Catalina.

She won the belt from Flammer at TripleMania, so she is still just weeks into her first reign, but Perez is looking to dethrone her and bring new gold to Judgment Day.

This is going to be a fun and competitive match, but the outcome seems clear. WWE has already started featuring Catalina on NXT and the main roster since she won the belt, so she has clearly won management over and become a priority.

WWE is going to want to keep her looking strong, so she is going to have a successful title defense this weekend against an opponent who is capable of bringing the best out of her.

CM Punk will appear at his first Worlds Collide event this weekend when he teams with Rey and Americano to take on Dirty Dom, Omos and McDonagh.

This is one of those matches that might seem a bit random to throw Punk into, but adding his main event status to the show can't be seen as a bad thing.

Not only does this continue Dom's feud with Americano, but it also brings him and his dad back together after not sharing a ring for quite some time.

This match feels built to give the crowd a happy ending, so the clear choice is Punk, Rey and Americano scoring the win, with McDonagh likely taking the fall so Omos and Dom can remain somewhat protected.

Worlds Collide: The Lucha Bros vs. Los Perros Del Mol

Penta and Rey Fenix have been kept apart for most of their WWE careers thus far, but The Lucha Bros will reunite this weekend when they take on Daga and Berto, who are part of a stable that goes by the name Los Perros Del Mol in AAA.

Even with LPDM holding the AAA trios titles, this feels like a slam dunk for Penta and Fenix.

Penta has been pushed hard in recent weeks as a potential top star, and Fenix has been gaining momentum, too. Their reunion will be seen as a special moment for this event, so having them lose wouldn't help anyone.

This is the only men's singles match on the card, and it's sure to be a banger. Lee and Cartwheel are both gifted high-flyers who might just steal the whole show. As great as Jack is, Lee feels like a higher priority for WWE at the moment.

This eight-person tag match is almost guaranteed to deliver some entertaining action. Either team could realistically win because the result won't have a big impact on future booking, so the best choice would be to give the babyface team the W to pop the crowd.

Prediction: La Parka, Mr. Iguana, Adelicious and Mascarita Sagrada

This women's trios bout features some talented performers, but the only outcome that makes sense is Fatal Influence getting the win. If the team that walks into this match with the U.S. and tag titles ends up losing, it's going to damage their brand.

Axiom vs. Mini Vikingo vs. EK Prosper vs. Je'Von Evans

This fatal 4-way features talent from across AAA, NXT, Raw and SmackDown, so the winner gets to take some bragging rights back to their respective brand. This is going to be a fast-paced and exciting match regardless of the outcome.

With Evans gaining momentum heading into Money in the Bank, giving him the victory is the most logical decision.

After a dominant run as the women's tag team champions, Megan Bayne and Lena Kross lost the belts to Jamie Hayter and Alex Windsor. Their rematch will up the stakes with a Street Fight, but the outcome will be the same. Giving the Birds a definitive win will cement their status as the new top duo in the division.

Kofi and Austin Creed only just debuted at All In when they won the Trios Championships alongside Swerve, so having them drop the titles so soon would be counterproductive to their push. Ricochet and Gates of Agony will give them a great challenge.

Steven Borden has only had a few matches in his short career, but AEW is clearly putting him on the fast track to success, so earning a tag title shot with Allin seems like a very real possibility. Fletcher and Knight will make great foils for them and put on a fun show, but Allin and Borden will earn the right to face whoever leaves All Out as the men's tag champs.

Cope and Cage vs. FTR vs. The Young Bucks

The men's tag titles will be held above the ring in a Chairs, Ladders and Tables match featuring three of the top teams in AEW. Adam Copeland and Christian Cage are the current champions, but any of these teams winning seems possible.

FTR only just returned recently, so they don't need to jump right back into being the champions. If the Bucks are truly thinking about retirement as they claim, then giving them one last reign is the right choice.

Prediction: The Young Bucks win the titles

Two former world champions will compete for a shot at the title currently held by Mercedes Mone when Willow battles the woman she beat for the belt in the first place, Thekla. These two have built this feud into something even more personal than just a shot at the title, so it will likely be a very physical encounter.

Thekla is an incredibly entertaining performer, but Willow has the deeper story with Mercedes, so having her earn the title shot is the best way to go right now.

The TBS title will be on the line when Persephone holds an open challenge this weekend. There are plenty of current stars who would be great here, such as Queen Aminata or Athena, but this feels like the perfect place to debut an incoming act.

Kairi Sane is expected to arrive in AEW soon, and a great way to introduce her would be having her challenge for the TBS title. Britt Baker can help Persy cheat to win to keep Sane protected, but it would get a much bigger pop to have Kairi win gold in her debut.

Prediction: Kairi Sane wins the TBS title

One of the matches with the most potential to steal the show will see Andrade put the national title on the line against Pac. This is going to be a hell of a match, and while it would be great to see Pac get a singles title again, El Idolo is on too much of a hot streak to take the belt off him now.

Not only has he been great since winning the national title, but he currently has a guaranteed shot at the world title in his possession. Giving him a strong title defense at All Out will keep his push strong heading into the end of 2026.

Under normal circumstances, we would pick Okada to retain in this match, but something tells us Ciampa is going to end up leaving the PPV with a belt around his waist.

On Wednesday, Ciampa promised to bring a version of The Psycho Killer that nobody has ever seen before. It genuinely feels like AEW wants him to be successful, and giving him a big win over someone on the level of Okada would be a fantastic way to do that.

Prediction: Tommaso Ciampa wins the international title

The men's world title will be on the line when Will Ospreay battles his former Death Rider mentor, Jon Moxley.

Ospreay winning the belt in front of his home country at All In was a career-defining moment, but in some ways, Moxley feels like the final boss of his story.

Beating Omega won him the title, but beating Moxley is what will allow him to prove he deserves to lead AEW as its top champion.

Mox will push Billy Goat to his limits, but the champion will ultimately prevail and leave All Out with his first successful PPV title defense.

articles.title: Final Grades for Every NHL Team's 2026 Offseason
articles.summary: There are still some unsettled pieces of business in the NHL (specifically Dylan Larkin and Connor Hellebuyck), but by the time they are resolved, it will be too late to consider them part of the offseason. That is because the 2026-27 regular season starts next week.
articles.body:
There are still some unsettled pieces of business in the NHL (specifically Dylan Larkin and Connor Hellebuyck), but by the time they are resolved, it will be too late to consider them part of the offseason. That is because the 2026-27 regular season starts next week.

Now that the season is here, it is time for one more report card on how every team handled their offseason.

These are not grades for the entire roster or for where they stand as a team. It is simply a grade of what they did this summer and how it all fits into the short-term and long-term outlook for each team.

ANA | BOS | BUF | CAR | CBJ | CGY | CHI | COL | DAL | DET | EDM | FLA | LAK | MIN | MTL | NJD | NSH | NYI | NYR | OTT | PHI | PIT | SEA | SJS | STL | TBL | TOR | Utah Mammoth | VAN | VGK | WPG | WSH

The good news is they got all of their restricted agents signed, as Leo Carlsson, Cutter Gauthier, and Pavel Mintyukov are all under contract and are not missing any regular-season games. They also avoided losing any of them, even though they had to match Carlsson's offer sheet.

The bad news is it cost them way more money than they probably anticipated, ate up all of their salary cap space, cost them a good veteran player in Chris Kreider, and did not allow them to make any major moves to upgrade a defense that was a major liability throughout the 2025-26 season. That doesn't even get into the trade of forward Mason McTavish for two draft picks.

It's still an exciting team with a good core, and the playoffs should still be within reach, but it's hard to argue the roster is in a better position than it was at the end of the playoffs, given all of the departures. In terms of adding to the team, this was an underwhelming summer for general manager Pat Verbeek, and it might result in a step backward on the ice. How big of a step backward remains to be seen.

J.J. Peterka is going to add some much-needed goal-scoring help, and there are some intriguing young players here, James Hagens and Fraser Minten, who could be serious long-term pieces. The contract extension for Minten could also be the type of move that pays off in the long run and becomes an extremely team-friendly deal.

The concern is that the Bruins were a little too dependent on goalie Jeremy Swayman to bail out a poor defensive performance in 2025-26, and I'm not sure the additions of Will Borgen and Connor Clifton will remedy those issues.

David Pastrnak, Charlie McAvoy, and Swayman are an outstanding trio to build your foundation around, and there is a solid complementary cast of forwards around them. But Swayman will have to put together another monster year to continue masking those defensive flaws. He is capable of doing that. His play and Pastrnak's presence at the top of the lineup might be enough to get them back into the playoffs. But the ceiling is very low here beyond that.

The best thing the Sabres did this offseason was get a bunch of young players locked into deals that should be cap-friendly bargains in the coming years. Getting Zach Benson and Noah Ostlund signed to contracts that will total less than $14 million against the salary cap over the next seven years could be a huge win as the cap continues to climb. That will pay for itself in the long run, as long as they continue to progress as players.

But when it comes to additions and subtractions, this summer was more about losing than gaining.

They made a smart move to get a top-five pick for Bowen Byram without overpaying, but it does leave a hole on the blue line in the short term.

It's understandable why they didn't want to pay a 30-year-old Alex Tuch $10.5 million per season, but he's still a 30-goal scorer.

Outside of adding defenseman Olen Zellweger, there hasn't been much coming back in.

They are going to be banking on a lot of internal development and improvement to get back into the playoffs. They might get it. But the roster on paper, as of late September, looks marginally worse than the one at the end of the season.

A Connor Hellebuyck addition would certainly change that, however.

Pending Free Agents Who Could Get Traded

The Flames stockpiled a cupboard full of first-round draft picks during their rebuild, and they cashed in two of them to trade for former New Jersey Devils defenseman Simon Nemec, then signed him to a long-term deal worth $7.25 million per season against the cap.

It's an interesting move because, while Nemec still has a lot to improve as an all-around player, he has some offensive upside and is still young enough to fit into their rebuild. It might be a little bit of an overpay in the short term, even with the rising contracts around the league, but it wouldn't take much for him to outperform it. But he has to show that he can actually do that.

They also traded veteran forward Blake Coleman to the Minnesota Wild for veteran defenseman Jake Middleton and more future draft pick capital. It will not be a shock when Middleton is also flipped at some point this season.

This is still the very early stages of a rebuild, and a team that's not going to be very good this season, especially on offense. A lot of patience will still be required here.

They took a swing at signing veteran defenseman John Carlson by trading a sixth-round pick for his free-agent rights, but they were unable to get him to sign.

Restricted free-agent defenseman Alexander Nikishin also remains unsigned, and there does not appear to be an end in sight.

Aside from some minor depth moves, the only major order of business was getting captain and reigning Conn Smythe winner Jordan Staal to sign a one-year contract extension. It's a solid move because Staal obviously still has some juice and can be a big-game player. He is also a perfect fit for their style of play.

It's not a team that needs much, and it still has plenty of salary cap space and draft pick assets (not to mention young talent) to swing another blockbuster trade at any time.

I imagine they will try at some point this season.

Bowen Byram is a good player, and he will make them better.

I don't think he is going to improve them as much as they think he will.

I'm also not sure he's worth the No. 4 and No. 45 overall picks in the draft and a $12.5 million-per-year contract extension.

That is, expecting him to be a No. 1 defenseman. The problem is that if he were a No. 1 defenseman, he would not be on his third team before his 26th birthday.

He's more likely a pretty good No. 2 or 3 defenseman. And that's fine. But is that worth the price they paid? We will see.

The Connor Bedard contract extension is fine given the market and direction of the offseason, but it doesn't really make the team any better or worse. It was just a major order of business that needed to be done.

The Patrick Kane reunion is going to be good for PR and will generate some excitement, and it will give them some more offense, but Kane is a shell of the player he used to be, and it remains to be seen where or how he will fit here outside of a big-time power play producer.

This is still a mostly bad team, with a very young roster full of unproven players that are still trying to find their way in the NHL. Expect more growing pains.

By trading away Valeri Nichushkin, Jack Drury, and Ross Colton, the Avalanche lost a lot of pretty good depth pieces. Jaden Schwartz was a nice value signing and could be a good fit, but is he enough to offset the three departures?

They re-signed a trio of defensemen to new contracts, including a record deal for superstar Cale Makar. It's a huge contract (over $20 million per season), but he'll still probably be worth it.

I'm not as high on the re-signing of Brett Kulak for five years and $22.5 million total. Not because it's too much of an overpay, but mostly because I'm not sure if you need to sign a 32-year-old, third-pairing defenseman to a five-year deal. There doesn't seem to be much reward or upside there.

Brent Burns on a one-year deal is fine, especially at the price tag ($850,000).

The Avalanche are still a serious contender, but expect some regression in the standings.

The vibes around the Blue Jackets this summer were mostly negative.

There were concerns about whether Zach Werenski would even be playing here this season, and there is still some long-term doubt about his future.

Kirill Marchenko is not even really hiding the fact that he will not be re-signing there long-term.

And it took them until Sept. 24, less than a week before the start of the regular season, to get restricted free agent Adam Fantilli signed.

It's not great. But at least all of them are still here. For now.

They also added Valeri Nichushkin from Colorado for nothing but draft-pick compensation, which brings in a legitimate middle-six forward who should help. It's a nice move on its own, but I'm not sure how I feel about it as the centerpiece of an entire offseason for a team that missed the playoffs and had some really big needs.

Rick Bowness seems determined to change the mindset of this organization, and it's either going to result in him winning the Jack Adams Award for getting it into the playoffs, or he is going to make his season-ending press conference look calm and reasonable with the meltdown he eventually has.

Getting a healthy Roope Hintz back will be a huge addition, and his absence was no doubt felt in their first-round playoff exit.

But it's still a team that took a step backward this past season, did not advance after three consecutive trips to the Western Conference Final, didn't really add anything to the roster, and still has some big questions on the right side of the defense.

If anything, they actually subtracted from the roster by moving Mavrik Bourque to the Nashville Predators.

Making matters even more complicated, they were only able to get Jason Robertson signed to a one-year deal and are heading into a potential lame-duck year with him as unrestricted free agency looms after the season.

Their Stanley Cup window is still open, but the clock is ticking, and this offseason didn't really extend it.

That's how this whole operation comes across right now.

Dylan Larkin requested a trade at the start of the offseason, Steve Yzerman was removed/stepped aside as general manager, and now, with the season just days away, they still do not have a new general manager to run the team.

That has resulted in Larkin not being traded, with nobody actually knowing whether he still wants a trade, and the organization stripping him of his captaincy.

Restricted free agent defenseman Simon Edvinsson (who also happens to be one of their best and most important young players) remains unsigned because they haven't had a general manager to finalize a new deal with him.

Their big offseason additions before all of that chaos started were Viktor Arvidsson and Keegan Kolesar. Arvidsson is a solid addition, but that's not a difference-maker for a team that has missed the playoffs for a decade and keeps collapsing late in the season.

The depth is still sketchy, the roster is still mostly mediocre, and they are about to head into the season with an interim general manager. It's bad. Really bad.

When it comes to the PR nightmare they've created for themselves, they get an F for hiring Mike Babcock and signing Alex Formenton.

Babcock's hiring is so controversial that even franchise legend Mark Messier called it out and said he was horrified by the decision.

What makes these moves even more baffling is that neither Babcock nor Formenton looks like they can even make a positive impact on the ice. At least not based on anything they have done recently.

Babock hasn't won anything of relevance in the NHL in over 15 years, and most of his recent teams have badly underachieved in both the regular season and the playoffs. If you like third-place finishes in your division and first-round playoff exits, this is your guy.

That doesn't even get into the extensive list of burned bridges with former players he's accumulated over the years by treating everybody who isn't a superstar like complete garbage.

As for Formenton, he hasn't played in the NHL in years and was a mid-level player on a Swiss team just this past season.

But if the PR blunders and questionable additions aren't bad enough, it's still a team with some serious depth issues and a very questionable goalie situation.

When it comes to the former, they were outscored 55-86 in 5-on-5 play when neither Connor McDavid nor Leon Draisaitl was on the ice, which is one of the worst marks the team has had during the McDavid-Draisaitl era. That's a testament to how awful the depth was this past season because they have had some truly dreadful performances away from McDavid and Draisaitl over the years.

Is Ryan Shea replacing Darnell Nurse, and will a new coach (who, again, has not won anything in the NHL in over a decade) close that gap?

When it comes to the goalie situation, they are relying on Tristan Jarry, Frederik Andersen, and Devon Levi to keep pucks out of the net. Jarry can't be counted on because he has continued to struggle even after leaving Pittsburgh. Andersen is 36 years old and struggles to stay on the ice. Levi has always had promise, but has never been consistent in the NHL.

The whole thing just seems like a house of cards ready to topple over.

Getting a healthy Aleksander Barkov back is a win just by itself.

But adding Brady Tkachuk, while only having to give up (indirectly) Mackie Samoskevich off the NHL roster, is another huge win.

Tkachuk may have been miscast as the No. 1 guy in Ottawa, but coming into a situation in Florida where he can be the No. 2 or 3 guy is going to be perfect for him. And for Florida.

The goaltending is going to be the big question here, and that's the only thing dropping this from an A offseason down to an A-minus offseason.

Will Jacob Markstrom bounce back from an ugly season in New Jersey? Florida is betting on his ability to do so.

The rest of the team might be so good that he won't need to bounce back much. He doesn't need to steal games; he just needs to avoid losing them. It should be a reasonable bar to reach.

Their biggest addition was getting Mats Zuccarello on a one-year deal. In terms of value, it might end up being one of the bigger steals of the offseason. Even at his age, he can still play and produce, and the Kings needed more offensive punch. He will help.

But outside of that signing and Erik Haula's signing, they didn't really do much and are also dealing with the retirement of long-time captain Anze Kopitar.

That's not going to be enough to get this team through the first-round ceiling it keeps ramming itself into. It might not even be enough to get them back in the playoffs.

The Brandt Clarke re-signing, however, was a really strong move, and getting him at $7.4 million over the next five years should be a steal. That bumps the letter grade up a bit.

Blake Coleman is a really strong pickup and the type of two-way winger that contending teams need. He's getting older, but he can still bring a spark.

The downside to the offseason is that they didn't do enough to upgrade their center depth, and they gave Michael McCarron too much money, over too many years for what he does.

Until they get more center help, you have to wonder how high this team's ceiling actually is, and they still have the big question of what to do with defenseman Quinn Hughes hanging over their heads. He is in the final year of his contract, has not signed an extension, and everyone in the league seems to think it is inevitable that he will go to New Jersey after this season.

Montreal didn't really add much this offseason until very late in the game, when it pounced on Chris Kreider after Anaheim let him go.

Setting aside the awkwardness of adding perhaps the most loathed active NHL player among Canadiens fans, it's a great fit and a great bargain. Especially that late in the summer. They needed another middle-six winger, and Kreider not only brings offense but also plenty of experience and chaos to the lineup.

The offseason began with the Canadiens getting another key player (forward Ivan Demidov) signed to a long-term deal that is going to end up being well below market value for almost all of its duration. It was the perfect storm of getting him signed before salaries exploded, and also the Canadiens' core being willing to sign so cheaply (relatively speaking). That is a huge advantage in a salary cap league, and Montreal should be set up for sustained, long-term success.

Easily the weirdest offseason in the NHL.

If you look at all of the moves they made as singular moves, they were all really good value.

The additions of Ross Colton, Jack Drury, Nils Hoglander, and Mavrik Bourque add some quality depth, and they didn't really have to give up a lot to get them. But they are the type of additions a team with a Stanley Cup-contending core would make to round out a championship roster. And Nashville simply doesn't have that sort of core, so it's just kind of hard to get a sense of where they think they are and what they want to be.

It's not bad. Nothing here is bad. And the team isn't going to be bad.

It's just an interesting approach from a first-year general manager, Chris MacFarland, who's inheriting a pretty average team.

Seems like a high-floor, low-ceiling kind of season is on the horizon.

The only move this offseason that seemed negative was trading Luke Evangelista to New Jersey after a 56-point season with strong underlying numbers. That might come back to haunt them.

Very promising debut for first-year general manager Sunny Mehta.

The Devils needed to improve their depth around star forwards Jack Hughes and Nico Hischier, and they did that in a really solid way with Evan Rodrigues, Luke Evangelista, and Anthony Mantha.

Mantha scored 33 goals a year ago and signed for just $4.75 million per season on a two-year deal, while Rodrigues is one of the more underrated two-way forwards in the league. Evangelista was also a solid pickup from Nashville and should be a strong top-six winger.

They also got Hischier signed to a new long-term contract extension that should age wonderfully, while also getting a strong return for Simon Nemec in a trade with Calgary, which set them up with additional draft pick capital.

They still have some concerns in goal, and they need Hughes to stay healthy for once, but this is a potential playoff team if a few things go right. They also have four first-round picks over the next three years and seem to be in the driver's seat to get Quinn Hughes next summer.

Way too quiet an offseason for a team that missed the playoffs and needed more offense.

Mattias Maccelli is the only major addition, and it's hard to even quantify it as such.

Matthew Schaefer is going to be a superstar, and Ilya Sorokin is capable of winning the Vezina Trophy and putting the team on his back and carrying it in any given season. They are going to need him to do that again, and for Schaefer to come back even better in year two for them to have a chance.

I do like Peter DeBoer as a head coach and think he can get a little more out of this team. But since that hiring happened during the 2025-26 season it does not get included in the offseason grade.

The Rangers needed a lot of help after a brutally disappointing 2025-26 season, and they did a really good job of finding a lot of what they needed.

Pavel Dorofeyev is a legit top-line winger who can score 35 goals, and even though he's not the guy to drive his line, he is an outstanding finisher. Eeli Tolvanen and Oliver Bjorkstrand are also solid, under-the-radar additions, especially given the fact that they had some chemistry when they played on a line together in Seattle.

They also overhauled their defense with the additions of Sean Durzi (as part of the Vincent Trocheck trade) and Marcus Pettersson, giving them what should be a very good top-four with Adam Fox and Vladislav Gavrikov.

It's not a perfect team by any stretch, and it might still only be a fringe playoff team. But the playoffs are very much within reach, especially with a superstar goalie in Igor Shesterkin and a potential Norris-caliber defenseman in Fox. If those two guys have big years (and especially Shesterkin), there is some upside here.

Their center situation and the lack of team speed are still a concern, but this should be a very competitive team.

Brady Tkachuk forced their hands not only by asking for a trade mid-contract, but also by being willing to go to Florida to play alongside his brother.

Given that situation, getting William Eklund and two additional first-round picks out of it isn't terrible. Eklund is a good player with upside, and those additional picks can be used to restock the farm system or as additional trade bait (one of the picks they received from Florida was already used to acquire Eklund).

Keeping Jordan Spence was a nice piece of business, while they also re-signed Drake Batherson to a long-term contract worth over $10 million per season. The Batherson contract seems a little rich for the player he's been, but this offseason, especially the second half of it, is going to force us to start re-evaluating what contracts look like and what their value actually is.

Nobody made a bolder move this summer than the Flyers' offer sheet for Leo Carlsson. Had they pulled it off, it would have been a franchise-changing move and taken them to an easy A for the summer. But other than the offer sheet, which Anaheim matched, the offseason was mostly about locking up their own players, including Tyson Foerster, Jamie Drysdale, Trevor Zegras, and Dan Vladar.

Vladar's contract is the riskiest of them given his position and how much concern there should be over his ability to repeat his 2025-26 performance, but they did give themselves a potentially solid fallback option in Joseph Woll.

The Flyers are still very committed to their rebuild, and a lot of young talent is hitting the NHL. A lot of their success or failure this season will depend on the goalies and how much of a breakthrough they get from players like Porter Martone and Matvei Michkov.

There was some hope in Pittsburgh at the start of the offseason that maybe the Penguins could pull off a blockbuster move, but nothing ever came together.

Instead, this offseason looked very similar to the 2025 offseason, with some low-risk free-agent moves and a few low-risk, potentially high-reward gambles.

On paper, the team looks very similar to the one that made the playoffs in 2025-26, but with a core group that is another year older. There are some wild cards here that could shift the season in a couple of different directions. If Ben Kindel has a big second season, and if Egor Chinakhov proves the second half of the 2025-26 season was not a fluke, and if Nicholas Robertson can take advantage of an increased role, there is the potential for a really deep group of forwards.

What they really need is the goalie duo of Sergei Murashov and Arturs Silovs to show they are ready to carry the load for an NHL team. There is upside with them, especially Murashov, but they might be the biggest wild cards on the team. If they are good, the Penguins will be good. If they are not good, the Penguins might be a lottery team.

The best thing that happened to the Sharks this offseason was something completely out of their control — moving from No. 9 in the NHL Draft to the No. 2 spot thanks to some lottery luck. That allowed them to pick forward Ivar Stenberg, giving them another potential star forward to join Macklin Celebrini, Will Smith, and Michael Misa.

Their second-best move? Getting Celebrini signed to a long-term deal before having to worry about it next summer, when he would have been a restricted free agent.

Mason Marchment is a fantastic forward addition, but the defensive moves leave a lot to be desired.

Adding one of Jacob Trouba or Darnell Nurse would have been understandable.

Adding both, at a combined salary-cap hit of over $17 million per season, is harder to understand.

They will have the chance to score many goals as a team, but stopping opponents will still be a major concern. They took a big step forward in 2025-26 and at least competed for a playoff spot. Given that progress and the offseason moves, it is time to start expecting the playoffs.

They thought they had a deal for Jason Robertson, but there was one small hiccup in that plan. He didn't actually want to go there. That is a shame for Seattle because it absolutely needs a player like him, and they made a great effort to get him. It just didn't work out. Nothing you can do about that. You can't make a player want to join you if they have other plans.

They did end up adding Mackie Samoskevich from Florida and re-signing Bobby McMann, but they are not really franchise-shifting moves the way Robertson could have been. If anything, they are just more of what Seattle's roster is already loaded with: Good, but not great players.

Jordan Kyrou is out, but Connor McMichael and Mason McTavish are in to join a pretty solid core group of players that already includes Robert Thomas, Jake Neighbours and Jimmy Snuggerud.

There is still some question as to how good McTavish and McMichael actually are, but the Blues are taking a big bet that they can both reach their potential in St. Louis. If they are right, they have the makings of a pretty good top-six, especially after keeping Thomas, who remains one of the league's most underrated star-level players.

The Brandon Carlo addition on defense doesn't seem to have the same upside, and they still have a big question mark in goal with the Jordan Binnington and Joel Hofer duo.

The Lightning's core is still in place, but it's starting to look like that window is closing after another first-round exit.

They added some pieces around the edge this offseason, including forward Ilya Mikheyev and defenseman John Carlson.

Carlson is the most significant move because he is still a viable top-four option and can run a power play and generate offense from the back end. They also needed someone to replace Darren Raddysh after he was traded to the Toronto Maple Leafs in a sign-and-trade deal.

Solid moves. But the Lightning's success will ultimately come down to the returning core players.

Speaking of which, at what point do Lightning fans start getting concerned that Nikita Kucherov does not have a new contract extension? The Lightning have not been afraid to let go of franchise icons in the past. Would they do it again?

Lottery luck smiled on the Maple Leafs, landing them Gavin McKenna with the No. 1 overall pick, and there is a strong chance he becomes a superstar in Toronto. They didn't do anything to get him except be unexpectedly bad for a year and have some ping-pong balls bounce their way, but it's a huge addition.

As far as moves they had actual control over, defenseman Darren Raddysh and goalie Sergei Bobrovsky are the big ones.

They paid Raddysh over $8 million per season, and if he duplicates his 2025-26 performance, or even comes close, he will be worth every penny of that contract. At least for a few years. The question is whether he can do that again or if he reverts to the good, but not great, player he was for the two years prior to that performance.

He's a two-time Stanley Cup winner and a two-time Vezina Trophy winner. He's a Hall of Famer when he retires. But at 38 years old, is he still capable of playing at anything close to that level? Toronto is taking a $7 million per year gamble that he can. They need to be right.

Swapping out J.J. Peterka for Vincent Trocheck and Anders Lee takes away some of the potential excitement and dynamic goal-scoring, but it might make them a better overall team.

Trocheck is a perfect matchup center for what they needed, while Lee is still very capable of causing havoc around the front of the net and scoring some garbage goals.

With Logan Cooley, Dylan Guenther, and Clayton Keller already in place, plus a strong defense, this could be a sneaky contender in the Western Conference.

The big concern is going to be in net. They traded a first-round pick to get Sebastian Cossa from the Detroit Red Wings, but he is completely unproven and a total wild card.

This could be a sleeper destination for Connor Hellebuyck.

The Canucks have made a minimal effort to start a rebuild, trading Nils Hoglander and Marcus Pettersson for future draft picks, including a 2029 first-round pick.

They also brought in Brendan Gallagher to fill a roster spot and kept Elias Pettersson for at least the start of another season.

It's nothing exciting. It's minor deck-chair shuffling. This could be the worst team in the league, and it seems nowhere near a contender. It's hard to argue that this offseason really did much to help them in the short term or the long term.

They re-signed many veteran players, including captain Mark Stone and defenseman Rasmus Andersson, but made few outside additions.

Andersson's extension seems like a significantly bigger risk than the Stone deal, based on its length and the fact that Stone still looks like a better player.

Beyond that, it was a lot of subtraction from the roster, as Pavel Dorofeyev, Keegan Kolesar, and Kaedan Korczak were all traded, with only draft picks and defenseman Parker Wotherspoon coming back. None of that is an immediate upgrade.

Vegas still has a very good team, but goaltending is going to be a big question mark again, and the roster (on paper, at least) does not look as strong as it did when it was skating in the Stanley Cup Final.

The Capitals were good enough to be a playoff team a year ago, and in most years, they would have been a playoff team given the number of wins (43) and points (95) they finished with.

They were already set to improve with the return of a healthy Pierre-Luc Dubois after he missed most of the 2025-26 season, and then they added two more top-six forwards, Jordan Kyrou and Alex Tuch.

Kyrou and Tuch are two of the best forwards in the league at generating chances and offense off the rush, and their additions should help transform a Washington offense that had grown a little stale.

They have an elite goalie in Logan Thompson, a nice upcoming core of young players (Ryan Leonard, Justin Sourdif, Cole Hutson), and now a completely revamped top-six.

They should not only be a playoff team, but they might also have a chance to win the East.

They added Mario Ferraro and Stuart Skinner.

That is also not enough. It is not enough for where this team was a year ago; it is not enough given the needs the roster still had; and it is not enough given everything at stake this offseason.

Their best and most important player, Connor Hellebuyck, is not with the team and is suspended for not showing up after the team did not yet honor his trade request, and it seems it is only a matter of when, and not if, his Winnipeg tenure comes to an end.

It remains stunning how inactive this organization is under general manager Kevin Cheveldayoff and how little urgency there always seems to be.

Another team that is a dysfunctional mess this offseason. They are taking advantage of the loyal fans who fiercely support hockey and the team. None of this is good enough.

articles.title: Mr. Olympia 2026 Dates, Schedule, Prize Money, Top Bodybuilders and Predictions
articles.summary: For fans of professional bodybuilding and fitness competition, the pinnacle event of the year has arrived. Joe Weider's Fitness and Performance Weekend is already underway in Las Vegas, and its marquee event, the Mr. Olympia open, is right around the corner.
articles.body:
For fans of professional bodybuilding and fitness competition, the pinnacle event of the year has arrived. Joe Weider's Fitness and Performance Weekend is already underway in Las Vegas, and its marquee event, the Mr. Olympia open, is right around the corner.

Olympia Weekend actually got started early in the week with the men's and women's Olympia Amateur competitions, and the Superstar Kickoff Party was held on Thursday. However, the top IFBB events have yet to unfold.

Here's a look at the remaining schedule for Olympia Weekend, along with a preview of the Olympia Open and its top competitors.

Primary Locations: Las Vegas Convention Center and Palms Casino Resort, Orleans Arena

*The 2026 prize payout is expected to be announced during competition.

International Sports Hall of Fame Induction Ceremony

Mr. Olympia Open Preview, Top Competitors and Prediction

The Mr. Olympia Open is widely viewed as the top competition in men's bodybuilding and the biggest IFBB event of the year. Unlike the Mr. Olympia 212, it has no weight limit and brings the biggest and best competitors in the world.

The Mr. Olympia traces its origins to 1965, when Larry Scott won the inaugural competition. In 1977, even organizer Joe Weider resurrected the Sandow Trophy—which made its debut all the way back in 1901—as the top prize in bodybuilding.

Over the years, several legendary bodybuilders have become multi-time Mr. Olympia winners, including Sergio Olivia, Arnold Schwarzenegger, Lee Haney, Dorian Yates, Ronnie Coleman, Jay Cutler, and Phil Heath. In 2025, Derek Lunsford joined the list by winning his second Olympia Open title in three years.

Lunsford headlines a list of top 2026 competitors that is 22 deep. However, only a handful are likely to have a realistic shot at challenging Lunsford for the crown.

2024 winner Samson Dauda is probably the most notable challenger this year after taking an extended offseason to hone his physique and prepare for this event specifically.

"People are saying, obviously, wow, this is the best Samson. It's the biggest Samson, and it's on target to be the best," fitness coach Chris Aceto said in a YouTube video (h/t Doug Murray of Fitness Volt).

Andrew Jacked is another serious threat, one who some believe should have won last year's Olympia Open.

While Jacked finished third behind Lunsford and Hadi Choopan, he bounced back to win the 2026 Arnold Classic. While Dauda and Lunsford may have a slight edge during judging as former champions, Jacked has the goods to come out on top.

Nick Walker and Martin Fitzwater are other pros who should be considered among the early favorites.

While fans may get an early idea of who can win during the prejudging, there's a good chance that the winner won't separate himself until the finals. The prediction here is that Dauda peaks at the right time to recapture the title of Mr. Olympia.

articles.title: 5 Spicy Hot Takes Heading Into the 2026-27 NHL Season
articles.summary: We're just four days away from a brand-new NHL season, and the newly shortened preseason is flying by as intended.
articles.body:
We're just four days away from a brand-new NHL season, and the newly shortened preseason is flying by as intended.

With only one more weekend of exhibition games before the real thing, it's time to shift gears and really think about the season to be. There are plenty of questions to ask ourselves while we wait.

Will the 2026 No. 1 overall pick, Gavin McKenna, bring the Leafs back into relevance? Will the Senators make the playoffs for the third straight season, or will the loss of Brady Tkachuk prove too much to handle? Speaking of Tkachuk, will he be enough to bring the Panthers back to excellence?

As much as we love thinking practically, we know the season rarely ends up exactly how we expected. With that in mind, here are six spicy takes that just might pan out this season.

Two in One: The Hurricanes Will Go Back-to-Back with Connor Hellebuyck in Net

It's not the spiciest assertion in the world that the Canes will go back-to-back. They're a +750 to win the Cup again, according to FanDuel , good for second-best. The only major change to their roster was Freddie Andersen's departure, and they've got the deepest team in the league.

Still, they've got stiff competition. In the East, the Panthers are charged up and healthy after some much-needed r&r. Meanwhile, the Canadiens are just getting started with their young, threatening roster. It's going to be harder than it was to even make it out of the conference this season.

If they earn that trip back to the Cup Final, they'll probably face a tougher opponent than last year's Golden Knights. Who's to say what the Avalanche would've accomplished last postseason had Nathan MacKinnon and Cale Makar stayed healthy?

Luckily for the Hurricanes, they could improve the most important position on their roster. The best goaltender in the world just so happens to be available. Connor Hellebuyck requested a trade from the Jets ; he has a no-movement clause, and he has the perfect opportunity to win his first Stanley Cup with the Canes. The Canes also have the cap space and roster space to make this work in a way other contenders don't.

Jets GM Kevin Cheveldayoff is adamant that he'll be as patient as it takes to make sure the Jets get the most out of this deal, but again, they've only got so much leverage.

Matthew Schaefer Will Hit the 30-goal Mark

The Islanders are coming into the 2026-27 season with some work to do on their roster before a meaningful playoff run is on the horizon. Despite entering the playoff race a few times last season, their power play was unwatchable (ranked 30th in the league), reflecting a need for more effective scoring overall.

They're also struggling with center depth, and the defensive core's floor could use an upgrade.

All that being said, they've got one of the most exciting players in the league entering his sophomore season at just 19. Schaefer was a revelation from his rookie debut, speeding up the team's pace and jumping right into a No. 1 defenseman role. He averaged 24:41 minutes per game and put up 23 goals and 59 points in 82 games.

On the way to the first unanimous Calder Trophy in 33 years, he tied Brian Leetch's single-season rookie record for defensemen. The expectations for the kid are high, and sophomore seasons are full of inevitable growing pains, but he's got what it takes to become the tenth defenseman in NHL history to reach the 30-goal mark next season. This is especially true on an Islanders team still yearning for offense.

The Sharks Will Win the Pacific Division

Playoffs, schmayoffs. If the Sharks keep going on the trajectory that saw them improve by 34 points last season, they're coming for the entire Pacific Division.

Let's take a look at the competition. The Canucks, Kraken, and Flames? Not much to worry about on this front, folks. Meanwhile, the Kings aren't getting any younger, and the Ducks could probably stand to get a bit older.

The top competition for the Sharks in the Pacific will be the Golden Knights and the Oilers, two teams that are perpetually at the top of the division due to their overall weakness. The Oilers are going to be hit-or-miss with the desperation moves they've made ahead of the last year on Connor McDavid's bridge deal, and the Golden Knights had to let their top goal scorer walk in the off-season with no replacement.

If there's any year for the Sharks to not just make the playoffs, but thrive in the division, it's this one. And if there's anyone to lead them there, it's Macklin Celebrini after a huge breakout year and a matching contract.

Pending Free Agents Who Could Get Traded

Penguins and Caps Face off in the Playoffs for the Last Time in the Crosby/Ovechkin Era

Look, you came here for some spicy takes. The likelihood of the Penguins and the Caps both making the playoffs in the packed East, let alone drawing each other in a matchup, isn't massive.

But we're saying there's a chance, and there's a real possibility we'll get to see Alex Ovechkin and Sidney Crosby face off in one last postseason.

The Capitals just narrowly missed the playoffs last year, and now they're back with serious additions like Alex Tuch and Jordan Kyrou. On the Penguins' side, Crosby, Evgeni Malkin, and Erik Karlsson each have just one season left on their contracts — you know they're giving it their all one last time.

Both teams have done a solid job at keeping their legends in the playoff race while keeping an eye on the future, and it's only right if we're rewarded with one last playoff series between Crosby and Ovechkin.

The Panthers' Big Anticipated Comeback Ends in More of a Meow Than a Roar

The Panthers had a rough 2025-26, but it was completely understandable: Aleksander Barkov was ruled out for the entire season before it even started, Matthew Tkachuk was out for half of it, and a laundry list of their other top players were out throughout the season.

The players who weren't injured? They were exhausted from three Cup Final appearances in three years, including two back-to-back wins that required two Game 7s.

They're coming back this season with much of the same core, save for a big departure of Sergei Bobrovsky. That menacing core is finally all healthy, and now Brady Tkachuk is in the fold to make it even scarier.

Still, it's going to be harder than it seems to jump back into the playoff race in the East. The competition is better than it was two seasons ago, with plenty of young, hungry talent as the Panthers get older. The key players who have missed significant time will need to get into playoff form fast if they want this season to end with a roar, not a meow.

articles.title: La 'TriArmada' busca hacer historia en casa en la Gran Final de Pontevedra
articles.standfirst: Ocho españoles disputarán las carreras Élite de la Gran Final de las Series Mundiales con el objetivo de pelear por el podio. El sábado compiten ellas, el domingo ellos
articles.summary: Ocho españoles disputarán las carreras Élite de la Gran Final de las Series Mundiales con el objetivo de pelear por el podio. El sábado compiten ellas, el domingo ellos
articles.body: Pontevedra ya está preparada para decidir los títulos mundiales de las Series Mundiales de Triatlón 2026 y lo hará con una importante presencia española en las dos carreras Élite. Cuatro hombres y cuatro mujeres formarán finalmente la representación española en las pruebas que se disputarán este sábado 26, la femenina, y domingo 27 de septiembre, la masculina, ambas a partir de las 18:00 horas. En categoría masculina, David Cantero, Alberto González, Roberto Sánchez Mantecón y Antonio Serrat serán los encargados de representar a España, mientras que en categoría femenina lo harán Sara Guerrero, Marta Pintanel, Noelia Juan y María Casals. El objetivo pasa por pelear por las medallas y cerrar la temporada con un gran resultado en casa. El valenciano David Cantero ha firmado una gran temporada, con un reciente segundo puesto en las WTCS de Weihai. Además ha cosechado una victoria en la Copa del Mundo de Lanzarote y un cuarto puesto en la WTCS de Quiberón. Alberto González también ha mantenido una gran regularidad en Series Mundiales con un quinto puesto en Londres, un octavo en Hamburgo y un noveno en Weihai. A ellos se suman Roberto Sánchez Mantecón, bronce en el Campeonato de Europa de Tarragona y undécimo en la Copa del Mundo de Haikou, y Antonio Serrat, cuarto en el Europeo de Tarragona y decimosexto en la WTCS de Londres. El gallego, además, formó parte del equipo español que terminó séptimo en el Campeonato del Mundo de Relevos Mixtos de Hamburgo. Entre las españolas, Marta Pintanel ha sido una de las principales protagonistas de la temporada, con un reciente séptimo puesto en la WTCS de Karlovy Vary hace dos semanas, un cuarto puesto en la Copa del Mundo de Lanzarote y una duodécima posición en el Campeonato de Europa de Tarragona. También fue integrante del equipo español que conquistó el bronce la prueba de Relevos Mixtos de Quiberón. Sara Guerrero, por su parte, llega después de lograr un cuarto puesto en la Copa del Mundo de Chengdu en el mes de mayo. Más allá de la actuación española, Pontevedra será el escenario de las dos carreras que decidirán los títulos mundiales de 2026. En categoría femenina, Cassandre Beaugrand, con cuatro victorias en cuatro carreras, parte como líder destacada con 4.000 puntos, 225 más que la británica Beth Potter. La sueca Tilda Månsson es tercera y la alemana Lisa Tertsch cuarta. La francesa necesita únicamente terminar en el podio para asegurarse matemáticamente el título mundial. Pero las últimas Finales han demostrado que la clasificación puede cambiar radicalmente en una sola carrera. Beth Potter remontó en 2023 para conquistar el Mundial y Lisa Tertsch protagonizó en 2025 la mayor remontada de la década, recuperando 289 puntos para proclamarse campeona. Además hay que destacar a nombres como la británica Georgia Taylor-Brown, las francesas Leonie Périault y Emma Lombardi, la luxemburguesa Jeanne Lehair y la estadounidense Taylor Spivey que también podrían pelear por ganar la carrera. La carrera masculina presenta un escenario diferente. Vasco Vilaça y el campeón en 2025, Matthew Hauser, llegan a Pontevedra separados por 354 puntos y, a priori, se jugarán el campeonato mundial entre ambos. El portugués lidera la clasificación con 3.850 puntos, mientras que el australiano, vigente campeón del mundo, suma 3.495. Vilaça será campeón del mundo si termina entre los cinco primeros. Hauser necesita ganar la Gran Final y que el portugués termine sexto o peor. Ricardo Batista, tercero de la general, conserva todavía opciones matemáticas, pero necesita ganar y que Vilaça termine decimotercero o peor y Hauser séptimo o peor. El duelo por el Mundial tendrá además varios protagonistas capaces de alterar la carrera. El francés Dorian Coninx, quinto de la general, ya sabe lo que significa ganar en Pontevedra: conquistó aquí la Gran Final de 2023 después de remontar 511 puntos en la clasificación. También estarán el británico Alex Yee, campeón olímpico y mundial en 2024, el neozelandés Hayden Wilde, ganador de la Final de 2024, y el húngaro Csongor Lehmann. El fin de semana también decidirá a los países campeones del mundo en los Relevos Mixtos de Triatlón Paralímpico y de la categoría Junior/Sub 23, que se disputarán el domingo por la mañana. Pontevedra vuelve a convertirse en el escenario decisivo del triatlón Mundial al acoger por cuarta vez desde 2019 una gran competición de World Triathlon, ya que fue sede de los Campeonatos del Mundo Multideporte de 2019 y 2025, además de la Gran Final de las Series Mundiales de 2023.

articles.title: CM Punk, Cody Rhodes Are Misranked and Top Takeaways From The PWI Top 500 List
articles.summary: MJF topped the 2026 PWI 500, but this year's top ten will still give wrestling fans online plenty to debate about.
articles.body:
MJF topped the 2026 PWI 500, but this year's top ten will still give wrestling fans online plenty to debate about.

Pro Wrestling Illustrated releases its annual list of the top 500 pro wrestlers in the world every fall. Securing the coveted top spot and the cover of the legendary magazine has become a celebrated accomplishment.

Maxwell Jacob Friedman will join an esteemed list that includes all-time greats like Hulk Hogan, Bret Hart, Shawn Michaels, Stone Cold Steve Austin, Kurt Angle, John Cena, A.J. Styles, Kenny Omega, and Kazuchika Okada.

As usual, hardcore fans will head to social media to dispute the results and plead their case for their favorites. We have some qualms with the list, but it all makes for fun debates.

For those who may not know, the PWI 500 is a kayfabe list that evaluates wrestlers based on the following criteria:

In-ring achievements: Win/loss records, championships, tournaments, and key contests won.

Influence: Visibility and prestige within a promotion and/or the industry.

Technical ability: Quality of moves, matches, and in-ring storytelling during a period.

Competition: Success against the most varied and highest-quality field of opponents.

Activity: Minimum 10 singles matches total; or, barring this, six such matches in separate months.

The evaluation period ran from Aug. 1, 2025 to July 31, 2026. The top 10 wrestlers on this year's list include:

You can find the full list of 500 wrestlers in the December 2026 issue of Pro Wrestling Illustrated. Digital copies are available on the publication's website .

It's hard to argue that Friedman doesn't deserve the number one spot. The three-time AEW World Champion has delivered some of his best performances over the past year and has emerged as a bona fide draw.

Whether you like him or not, he was the most consistently impactful top star during the evaluation period. His 2025 feud with "Hangman" Adam Page helped to reinvigorate the product, and he was an effective foil to Omega and Will Ospreay in the lead-up to All In: Texas.

Yota Tsuji has also had a tremendous year as the reigning IWGP Heavyweight Champion. One could even contend that he shouldn't have been higher on the list because his output since Wrestle Kingdom 20 has been incredible. He was the most entertaining competitor to watch in the G1 Climax.

Oba Femi and Trick Williams deserved recognition for their breakout year on WWE's main roster. The Ruler is the most effective NXT call-up in recent memory and the future of the company. Similarly, Penta , who ranked 24th, has had a fantastic transition to the bigger stage on Raw.

Místico is still new to some mainstream fans, but he is the biggest box office draw in Mexico. His work with AEW and NJPW was entertaining, but he earned fourth place as the luchador who helped CMLL become a powerhouse again.

Cruz Montana landed surprisingly high at number 13. However, he successfully reinvented himself as a single competitor with TNA and became a two-time world champion. At number 14, Callum Newman , 23, turned heads as the youngest wrestler to win the New Japan Cup and IWGP heavyweight title.

Kevin Knight landed at 24, following a phenomenal run with the TNT Championship. This year, he successfully defended his title against three former world champions and headlined AEW Redemption against Omega.

Darby Allin arguably deserved a higher spot than 12 following his first AEW world title win to close Dynamite: Spring BreakThru. His reign only lasted 39 days, but his seven defenses were some of the best television matches of the year.

Conversely, Jon Moxley's absence from the top 10 was particularly glaring. Considering his 2025 Continental Classic win and 271-day reign as champion, you would think he would rank higher than 19.

Mox has been dominant since the C2, pulling off upset wins over high-profile opponents during the evaluation period. Roman Reigns' omission from the PWI 500 also sparked some outrage online.

Although The Tribal Chief has produced three exceptional outings in 2026, he didn't compete in enough matches to meet the criteria. Still, his most avid fans would say that his seven matches, Royal Rumble win, and five-star WrestleMania main event appearance made him the most relevant top star in the industry.

CM Punk Should Rank Higher Than Cody Rhodes

Surprisingly, Cody Rhodes ranked second after his most underwhelming tenure as a main eventer. The second-generation star held the number one spot for two consecutive years, from 2024 to 2025.

Rhodes deserved it because he was WWE's biggest star during that time, but it's hard to justify his position this year. Curiously, CM Punk is below him at third and has had a much better run since August.

The Second City Saint has secured three world title wins during the evaluation period. His match against Gunther at SummerSlam in 2025 exceeded expectations. This year, Punk vs. Reigns ended WrestleMania weekend with a match-of-the-year contender.

Even more, his return in July to win the Undisputed WWE Championship elevated SmackDown's main event scene. Punk may be polarizing, but he has eclipsed Rhodes as the blue brand's most prominent Superstar. The American Nightmare certainly belongs in the top 10, but not that high.

The 21-year-old is set to make her Test debut off the bench after impressing for Munster during the Women's Interprovincial Championship.

articles.title: Lewis Hamilton faces Baku investigation as Ferrari insider reveals what is changing for the seven-time champion
articles.summary: Lewis Hamilton was investigated after a tense incident with Liam Lawson during FP2 at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
articles.body: Lewis Hamilton was investigated after a tense incident with Liam Lawson during FP2 at the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. The Ferrari driver was running slowly when Lawson approached him near Turn 19 in Baku.Lawson was forced to react and described the situation as “f***ing dangerous” over team radio. Hamilton finished fifth in the session, while Lawson ended 12th. The incident comes as Hamilton continues his first full season with Ferrari. His adjustment to Maranello has also been discussed by former Ferrari race engineer Jock Clear, who believes the seven-time world champion is now having an important influence on the team.Lewis Hamilton’s Ferrari influence comes under the spotlight after Baku incidentLewis Hamilton was summoned by the stewards following the FP2 incident with Liam Lawson for an alleged breach of the FIA regulations relating to impeding.Lawson came across Hamilton’s Ferrari as the Mercedes driver-turned-Ferrari star was travelling slowly through the final section of the Baku circuit. The Racing Bulls driver reacted immediately, “Oh my god, that’s so f***ing dangerous. Oh my god, dude, that is so dangerous.”The incident added another talking point to Hamilton’s Azerbaijan weekend. The Briton has already faced criticism for similar situations earlier in the season.However, his current Ferrari chapter is about more than incidents on track. Former Ferrari race engineer Jock Clear has offered an insight into Hamilton’s role inside the team and his relationship with Charles Leclerc while speaking to GrandPrix247.Notably, Clear worked with Hamilton earlier in his career and spent several years coaching Leclerc at Ferrari. He believes Hamilton’s arrival can help Ferrari and also accelerate Leclerc’s development as a potential world champion.According to Clear, Hamilton brings more than speed and race experience. He believes Leclerc can learn from the seven-time champion about leadership, team building and the political side of Formula 1.“That’s the bigger picture of building the team around him and getting momentum,” Clear told GrandPrix247.com.Clear also believes Hamilton is still adapting to Ferrari after a difficult first year. He described the transition as a process that requires time and patience.He also rejected the idea that Hamilton automatically has the status of Ferrari’s number-one driver. He expects Leclerc to continue challenging his experienced teammate.The comments show the competitive dynamic inside Ferrari. Hamilton has the experience of seven world championships, while Leclerc has spent years establishing himself as Ferrari’s leading driver.Clear believes both can push each other forward. He said, “Charles sees that and Lewis sees that. I think they’ll continue to work well together.”For Hamilton, the focus now returns to the Azerbaijan Grand Prix. articles.title: Knicks' Karl-Anthony Towns gets major contract extension timeline, will have to make 'sacrifice'
articles.summary: The New York Knicks and Karl-Anthony Towns are trying to come to an agreement on a contract extension. However, it doesn't seem like it will happen anytime s...
articles.body:
The New York Knicks are gearing up for another run at the NBA Finals after reaching the championship series last season. For the most part, the organization has the same core coming back.

"Talks have stagnated between the New York Knicks and Karl-Anthony Towns on a contract extension, and an agreement is considered unlikely as the team begins training camp next week, sources told ESPN on Wednesday. The sides have spent extensive time discussing a potential extension during the offseason, but there has been no movement lately in negotiations," ESPN wrote.

While there seems to be no movement toward a deal right now, Towns is willing to take a pay cut in an extension.

"Towns is willing to play on a deal that isn't the max to help New York, per league sources, but it's still unclear how much he's willing to leave on the table. This is likely the last massive contract opportunity for Towns, who turns 31 during the season," The Athletic's James Edwards III said.

The center played a crucial role for the Knicks, including in their efforts to slow down Victor Wembanyama . NBA insider Brett Siegel doesn't think an agreement will come anytime soon, and if it does, he believes Towns is going to have to make a sacrifice.

"Karl-Anthony Towns is going to have to take a discount if he wants to remain with the Knicks. Jalen Brunson did so for them to win a championship… It's gonna have to be Towns to be the one to sacrifice… I don't think an extension gets done anytime soon," Siegel said.

There is no clear answer in sight in terms of what is actually going to happen. There is no doubt that Towns wants to remain in New York; it is just a matter of how far he is willing to come down financially.

The Knicks don't want to lose their starting center, but they also don't want to overpay, which could put them in a difficult position when it comes to other contracts. Ultimately, the decision could come down to how much Towns is willing to sacrifice financially, and Siegel believes that choice may not come anytime soon.

articles.title: Rayan denies Australia famous win over Brazil with last-gasp equaliser
articles.summary: Australia were denied a famous victory over Brazil as Rayan’s stoppage-time header rescued a 1-1 draw in Queensland.The Socceroos made a bright start, with N...
articles.body:
Australia were denied a famous victory over Brazil as Rayan 's stoppage-time header rescued a 1-1 draw in Queensland.

The Socceroos made a bright start, with Nestory Irankunda and Conor Metcalfe causing problems for the visitors, while Patrick Beach was also called into action to keep Brazil at bay.

Brazil thought they had taken the lead shortly before half-time when Estevão found the net, but the goal was ruled out by VAR after Bruno Guimarães was adjudged to have fouled Harry Souttar in the build-up.

Australia continued to threaten after the break and finally got their reward in the 68th minute. A foul on Paul Okon-Engstler presented Irankunda with a free-kick, which the winger brilliantly curled into the top corner beyond Hugo Souza .

Tony Popovic's side looked set to hold on for a memorable win, but Brazil found a late equaliser. Raphinha 's corner picked out Rayan , whose powerful header beat Beach in the 95th minute.

articles.title: Chiefs news: Travis Kelce reveals what Patrick Mahomes drank before KC's WK 2 win
articles.summary: Before he led his team to a Week 2 win over the Indianapolis Colts, quarterback Patrick Mahomes was seen drinking something in the locker room, and his Kansa...
articles.body:
Before he led his team to a Week 2 win over the Indianapolis Colts , quarterback Patrick Mahomes was seen drinking something in the locker room, and his Kansas City Chiefs teammate Travis Kelce gave his two cents on what it was.

Talking about the now-viral moment before the game , Kelce conceded that "it looks like some Limoncello or somethin', man," before saying he didn't know.

"Who knows; maybe he's got [Steve Spagnuolo's] wife Maria's famous Limoncello, nice little [click noise], get you goin', get the blood pressure goin'," he added. "I would say that that's the pickle juice that we have. He's just drinkin' electrolytes; it's hot out here, it's humid out here. He wants to make sure he gets those electrolytes. Pickle juice is one of the most famous things to help you not cramp during the game and keep you hydrated, so he's just taking a quick shot of that pickle juice, baby."

Chiefs' Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce turned back the clock in Week 2 win vs. Colts

Whatever Mahomes drank helped him out in Week 2. He had an MVP-like performance, throwing for 382 yards and three touchdowns without a turnover.

Kelce led the Chiefs with nine receptions and 101 yards. He caught his first touchdown of the season after the Chiefs' defense intercepted Daniel Jones .

The Chiefs needed overtime to beat the Colts, but they got the job done. They will now visit the winless Miami Dolphins in Week 3 before playing the Las Vegas Raiders the following week.

Mahomes is coming off a torn ACL injury suffered in December 2025. He returned in time for the Chiefs' Week 1 game over the Denver Broncos . It wasn't perfect, but Kansas City pulled out the win. Through two games, Mahomes has thrown for 566 yards, five touchdowns, and one interception. He has also rushed for 40 yards and a touchdown.
