articles.title: World Grand Prix Darts: Will Luke Littler successfully defend his title? Luke Humphries, Gerwyn Price and Ross Smith in the mix
articles.summary: Will Luke Littler successfully defend his title? Luke Humphries, Gerwyn Price and Ross Smith are all in the mix for the double-in, double-out tournament in Leicester; you can watch World Grand Prix Darts live on Sky Sports from September 28 - October 4
articles.body:
Littler will be hoping the home crowd at Leicester's Mattioli Arena is more welcoming after the two-time world champion was booed and whistled at during the World Series of Darts Finals exit in Amsterdam earlier this month .

The 19-year-old headed into the tournament chasing a historic clean sweep after winning the first six major titles of the season but suffered a crushing 10-4 defeat to Jonny Clayton in the last eight .

Stephen Bunting backed Littler, saying he has "changed" darts since bursting onto the scene a few years ago.

"It's really hard, isn't it? Obviously, Luke is the best player in the world. For whatever reason, the crowd got on his back, they didn't want him to do the [clean sweep]," said Bunting.

"He was probably on edge, anyway, going into [the tournament]. Maybe in Germany, in Belgium, I've had it a few times where the crowd has whistled out.

"If you let the crowd know they're getting to you, it can be 10 times worse. It's a hard one to say, but I don't like the whistling. I'd rather have someone shouting abuse at me than whistling.

"It's a horrible noise to hear when you're trying to concentrate. But I understand it'll keep happening, no matter how much we talk about it.

"Punishments need to be brought in, maybe. Until that happens, it'll keep happening."

Littler takes on Luke Woodhouse in the first round and if he wins he will go on to play either Nathan Aspinall or Kevin Doets in round two.

Luke Humphries lost the World Grand Prix final two years ago but 'Cool Hand Luke' must at least match that run this time, otherwise he will surrender second place in the world rankings to Gian van Veen.

The former world champion opens his campaign against Dave Chisnall, with a potential second-round showdown against Chris Dobey or Jermaine Wattimena.

Humphries, who suffered a shock defeat to Mike De Decker in the 2024 final, only returned to competitive action at the end of August for the first time since his shock round-one exit to Cameron Menzies in the World Matchplay on July 20 and went on to win Players Championship 28 before defeat to Littler in the final of the Czech Open .

Humphries said: "I'm going to get back on the practice board at home as much as I can now and I'm going to dedicate the rest of the year to trying to be my best and trying to push Luke - and not just Luke, but everyone else because I want to stay at No 2.

"Whether that happens or not, I'm going to fight for it because I'm going to try my best."

James Wade also has significant prize money on the line at the World Grand Prix while Ross Smith heads into the tournament in the form of his life having produced a masterclass to destroy Gerwyn Price and end his four-year wait for second major title after winning the World Series of Darts Finals in Amsterdam .

Wade ended a decade-long wait for a European Tour title as he beat Smith in the final of the Flanders Darts Trophy earlier this month and heads to Leicester in fine fettle.

"Wadey this year, last year even, he's just someone that you just can't really bet against," Polly James said on the Love The Darts podcast . "His scoring power, his doubling, just everything. And when it's on and he's in a good mood up for it, he could easily win this."

Paul Nicholson added: "What's he going to do next? Win the Worlds? We've talked about how the fact he's never going to win that. Well, maybe he could now."

Smith, who told Love The Darts he feels ready to play in the Premier League, has appeared in two major finals and has won both after winning the recent World Series of Darts Finals to add to his European Championship in 2022.

Nicholson, nicknamed 'The Asset', advised former trucker Smith to "stay energised" and "stay sharp" and "keep believing" as he prepares to face Cameron Menzies in the opening round of the World Grand Prix.

"When he wins in Amsterdam, it's not an accident because he's one of the best players in the world right now," said Nicholson. "He's doing a lot right."

Gerwyn Price will be looking to end a four-year wait for another major crown at the same tournament where he had last lifted one.

Meanwhile, six-time World Grand Prix winner Michael van Gerwen is a player who is struggling for form having recently suffered a first-round exit at the World Series of Darts Finals.

Speaking ahead of Van Gerwen upcoming World Grand Prix game with Ryan Joyce, Nicholson questioned whether he will ever find his best form again.

"As he slips down the rankings, we should say, 'you're not finished'. He has people in his corner but what are you going to do about it? Ultimately it's up to him. The definition of a comeback is what you do on the stage in moments and those moments are fewer than before."

Other players to watch out for are Wessel Nijman, who is enjoying an outstanding season, already winning four Players Championship titles and two Euro Tour titles, and fellow Dutchman Kevin Doets - who is one of the names every player hopes to avoid in the draw - including his first-round opponent Nathan Aspinall.

articles.title: Joe Burrow refreshingly comes to defense of embattled Bengals teammate
articles.summary: Bengals QB Joe Burrow plays defense for his teammate.
articles.body:
Cincinnati Bengals offensive tackle Orlando Brown Jr. has been under some serious heat to start the season.

In a fun twist, it's Joe Burrow rushing to stand in front and protect Brown.

With his Bengals at 2-0, Burrow fielded questions during his weekly presser and made a point to defend Brown from some of the online criticism making the rounds.

"I think Orlando was pretty good (in Houston ). There were a couple of sacks that weren't in his control at the end of the day," Burrow said, according to Geoff Hobson of Bengals.com. "There are a lot of different things that go into pass protection that's not just on the offensive line…That's what you don't see in the media. There's very intricate details of pass protection. A guy expecting help here, a guy expecting help from a different spot. A lot of different things go into it that we would never explain to you guys."

Online and social media spaces tend to overly highlight Brown's struggles at times. It's notable when he had a bad rep in the preseason or over the first two games of the regular season. At times, it's almost similar to only thinking about cornerbacks when they surrender touchdowns in coverage.

With Brown, he's always been a bit of a streaky player who tends to struggle with speed rushers. His start to the season has been far from perfect, but his general body of work has always been above average. And when every offensive line tends to struggle against the Houston front seven, it's hard to overreact much to the Week 2 happenings.

Plus, like Burrow says, only the guys in the building know who really deserves the blame on sacks and pressures most of the time.

And in Cincinnati, specifically, Bengals fans know all too well just how much worse offensive tackle play can get, so it's probably especially nice to see Burrow using his platform to defend his guys.

articles.title: The Giants’ 2026 Season Looks Very Different Without Jaxson Dart
articles.summary: After a Week 1 win over the Cowboys, the Giants felt optimistic about their season outlook. Second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart played well and led the team...
articles.body:
After a Week 1 win over the Cowboys, the Giants felt optimistic about their season outlook.

Second-year quarterback Jaxson Dart played well and led the team to victory. The defense held a high-powered Dallas offense to just 20 points. The victory gave fans reason to believe this team could compete for a playoff spot.

However, they faced a very tough test in Week 2. They traveled to Los Angeles to take on the Rams, one of the top teams in the NFL. New York looked overmatched on Monday night, losing 28-6.

But the final score was not the biggest concern coming out of Los Angeles. It was the injury to the Giants' young quarterback.

Dart's season is over after further testing revealed a significant knee injury . He suffered damage to his PCL, MCL, and meniscus. The Giants went from feeling good about their season to facing major questions about their future at quarterback.

With their second-year signal caller sidelined for the rest of 2026, is the Giants' season already over?

The Giants' biggest concern coming out of Los Angeles is no longer whether Jaxson Dart will miss a few games. He will miss the rest of the season.

Dart sustained the injury on New York's opening possession and did not return. Further testing revealed that the injury was more serious than initially expected, ending what had been a promising start to his sophomore season.

This is a devastating blow for a Giants team that entered 2026 believing Dart could establish himself as its franchise quarterback. He opened the season by throwing three touchdown passes without an interception in a 28-20 victory over the Cowboys. One week later, his season is over.

Big Blue now has to turn to veteran quarterback Jameis Winston . Winston struggled on Monday night after coming in for Dart. He completed just 11 of 27 passes for 111 yards and one interception. New York did not score a touchdown in the game.

Winston will have to lead the Giants offense for the remainder of the season. It will be a major challenge. They built their offense around Dart and his ability to make plays with his arm and his legs. Winston does not have the same mobility. Now, the Giants have to adjust their entire offensive approach with him taking over.

Losing Dart does not mathematically end the Giants' season. They are still 1-1 and have 15 games remaining. However, it changes the expectations surrounding this team. The question is no longer whether Dart can lead the Giants to the playoffs. It is whether Winston can keep the team competitive enough to remain in the postseason race.

Winston's performance in Week 2 was not encouraging. But that does not mean he can't perform well going forward.

Winston is a former number one overall pick who has been in the league for 12 seasons. He has nearly 25,000 passing yards in his career. Winston has spent a lot of time as a backup, but he has also shown he can be a capable starter.

Above all, Winston is viewed as a great leader and veteran presence in the locker room. He was voted onto the Giants' eight-man leadership council before the season. Now, he will have to lead this young Giants team for the rest of the 2026 season.

Some of Winston's struggles against the Rams can be attributed to a lack of reps with the starters. With Dart sidelined, Winston will have more time to build chemistry with the first-team offense.

Fortunately for Winston, the tea, does have a solid group of playmakers.

Malik Nabers , Isaiah Likely , Malachi Fields, and Darnell Mooney give Winston several options in the passing game. They give Winston options at every level of the field. Running back Cam Skattebo can take pressure off of Winston with his ability to churn out yards. If Winston can develop a connection with these players, the Giants could still have a functional offense without Dart.

Additionally, New York needs their defense to step up. Matthew Stafford threw for 327 yards and four touchdowns against the Giants in Week 2. New York also struggled against the run. The Rams averaged 5.8 yards per carry.

Another issue has been the lack of pass rush. Big Blue has just one sack in two games. That is the second fewest in the league. The defense will need to make significant improvements if the Giants are going to remain competitive without Dart.

The Giants' Injury List Keeps Getting Longer

Unfortunately, Dart wasn't the only Giant to go down in Week 2.

Star wide receiver Malik Nabers suffered a shoulder injury at the end of the first quarter. He was able to return to the game, but was not effective. Nabers finished with just one catch for one yard on four targets. He said that his shoulder is "OK", but the Giants will continue to monitor the injury. If he has to miss any time, New York's offense would take a major hit.

Another player who got injured was left tackle Andrew Thomas . He exited in the fourth quarter with a groin injury. Luckily, his injury is not considered serious , and he has a chance to play in Week 3. Thomas has missed time before with injuries. He is the Giants' best lineman and they need him to stay on the field. He will be responsible for protecting Winston and helping create lanes for New York's running backs.

Pass rusher Brian Burns also got hurt in the fourth quarter. Burns suffered a low ankle sprain . He won't need surgery, but is expected to miss some time. Burns does not have a sack yet this year, but was great in 2025. He had a career-high 16.5 sacks and earned Pro Bowl and second-team All-Pro honors. Kayvon Thibodeaux and Abdul Carter will have to generate more pass rush in Burns' absence.

Ultimately, the Giants' season is not over, but it is very different from the one they envisioned. They entered 2026 expecting Dart to take the next step in his development. Now, his season is over after just two games.

The Giants can still compete, but their margin for error has changed dramatically. Winston, the rest of the offense and the defense will all need to step up if New York hopes to remain in the playoff race in 2026.

articles.title: Cole Palmer warned by Thomas Tuchel over latest ‘missed opportunity’ with England
articles.summary: The Chelsea star has impressed this season after missing out on the World Cup squad, but dropped out of the squad with load management cited as the reason
articles.body:
Cole Palmer has been warned by Thomas Tuchel over his England future after another "missed opportunity" following his latest withdrawal.

The Chelsea star was left out of the World Cup last summer but has impressed so far this season after a run of games for his club, forming part of an exciting attacking trio under Xabi Alonso.

But Palmer was among five players to drop out of the squad after his latest recall, with load management cited as the reason, leading Tuchel to admit that he may struggle to "rely" on the player without witnessing his form up close.

"For sure, it's a missed opportunity," Tuchel said ahead of England facing Spain in the Nations League. "It's another missed opportunity, it's just a fact, he misses way too many camps with injuries.

"I only want to rely on what I witness and see from my team. For that you have to be in camp, if you're not in camp, there's a next level to impress that you cannot achieve, you cannot do it unless you're with me on the pitch, so yes, it's a missed opportunity."

Tuchel also admitted frustration at the situation surrounding Palmer's availability.

"My understanding is he plays with this discomfort and pain and he cannot compete at the highest level with this pain and withdrew," Tuchel added.

" Chelsea informed us of this understanding, we're not managing load, I used the term of an international break, from the other side it's totally different. What we created, a competitive environment, but also one the players love to be in, walk through the door, love to train with each other, be with each other, that's what togetherness and brotherhood looks like.

"We will never compromise on that. We will never let this creep in, the feeling that players don't want to come. We focus on the players who absolutely want to play for England."

articles.title: Ferrari pinning hopes on rain to be Fuji leveller
articles.summary: Ferrari's prospects could be helped by rain at Fuji.
articles.body:
The 6 Hours of Fuji represents a crucial round in the race for the FIA World Endurance Championship titles, with the standings potentially shifting decisively – either to seal the deal or to throw the title race wide open.

However, a major uncertainty hangs over Japan in the form of the menacing clouds, though the heavy downpours that had hit in previous days stayed away during Free Practice, but still threaten to return on Saturday and Sunday.

This is what the Ferrari team have been focusing on; right from the start, they have sought to make the most of the dry track to gauge the performance of the 499P, a car not usually well-suited to the Japanese circuit, but which, in the rain, could find an unlikely ally to challenge its rivals – notably Toyota, Alpine and Genesis, who have particularly stood out today.

"Today was quite important because it's going to rain heavily tomorrow and on Sunday we might have mixed conditions, with a few downpours. So it was crucial to make the most of Free Practice to try and improve; then we'll see how things pan out in the wet," said Antonio Fuoco, speaking to journalists at Fuji, including Motorsport.com.

"We fitted the medium tyres this morning because the temperatures were already high and there wasn't much grip, but I don't think the track conditions will improve, and I always believe it's best to try things out for the race right from the start. Given there's a good chance of a wet or at least damp race, it was important to try something for dry conditions today.

"Wet qualifying? Honestly, I don't recall there ever having been one, so I think it'll be a first for everyone. We'll find out tomorrow what happens. In the meantime, we've seen that there are a couple of cars that look really strong, especially Alpine, but also Genesis. However, conditions can change quite a lot over the course of the weekend, so it's best to focus on ourselves and give it our all."

As mentioned, Ferrari has never enjoyed much success in the Land of the Rising Sun. This means making the most of every opportunity to try and secure a good result, perhaps even picking up some championship points that could prove crucial at the end of the year, as Antonio Giovinazzi points out.

#51 Ferrari AF Corse Ferrari 499P: Antonio Giovinazzi

"Let's just say we haven't come here with a magic formula: the car is the same, the tyres have changed, so we need to try and adapt a bit more to this situation. So far, we've struggled every year, doing just a tad better in 2025; we'll build on that and try to do our best," explains the driver from Puglia.

"We're aware that our car isn't the best on this circuit, even though we made a few small steps forward in 2025. But the others have improved too, such as Toyota and Genesis. Sector 3 remains a problem for us, but so does Sector 2, in some respects. Quite simply, it's difficult to find a good compromise, and it's been that way ever since the first year we came here.

"The races are long and a lot can happen; we'll see if, between now and Sunday, we can find solutions to improve our car. If we're not competitive in dry conditions, I hope it rains on Sunday.

"In the past, we've seen that even in difficult conditions, we've managed to pick up a few points in the end, as was the case in Brazil, for example. We must never give up, bearing in mind that the #51 car remains the best-placed in the drivers' standings to challenge for the title.

"In Austin, we picked up some points in the Constructors' Championship, whilst the #50 car scored in the Drivers' Championship. The #7 Toyota retired, which was a positive. We know it will be tough here, but we've always struggled at Interlagos too; yet this year we achieved a good result. Unfortunately, things didn't go too well for us in the #51 car at COTA, but never say never. We need to be smart with our strategy and pull everything together, trying to score as many points as possible."

Engineer Mauro Barbieri shared this view, providing an overview of the work carried out today, whilst naturally refraining from making any bold statements or predictions.

"The first practice sessions are always used to fine-tune the set-up and get to grips with the track. Apart from the #8 Toyota, the whole field has been fairly close together, but I wouldn't read too much into the lap times as the weather forecast for tomorrow suggests a high probability of rain.

"We're hoping it'll be wet in Free Practice 3, so we can optimise the set-up in those conditions too. But let's just say the situation is more or less the same as in previous years. Clearly, we're getting into a subject I can't really discuss.

"Let's just say that it seems something has been done to try and keep the field a bit closer together in terms of lap times, as we've seen throughout the season, but it's also true that overtaking is always difficult, even on the straights. That's why, in some races, we've seen cars adopt different strategies to get more laps on a clear track and avoid being held up by traffic. That's the downside of having lap times so close together.

"It would have been important to test them, given that the forecast is set to change for Saturday and Sunday; there might be times when the track is a bit damp and the soft tyres could come in handy.

"But we also need a benchmark for how they perform in dry conditions, because if they only last 20 laps instead of 50, it might be better to struggle a bit more in the early laps with the medium tyres, but be more competitive over the long run and with less degradation."

After the race, Ferrari has scheduled a day of testing on Tuesday 29th, but only as a 'roll-out' for the current 499P cars, which will then see out the season. There will be no further testing of the 2027 EVO version, which is expected to return to action in Barcelona on 20 October – at least according to the official calendar – although Barbieri has not revealed any further details.

"We thought this was the best way to rebuild the cars by fitting the new parts after the race, so as to carry out a sort of one-hour shakedown to check that everything is in order. After that, we'll send the cars to Barcelona, which is what we did in Austin before coming here.

"We won't be testing the updated version here in Japan, but we don't usually say when we'll be out on track for testing."

articles.title: NHL salary cap set for historic leap as new projection stuns league!
articles.summary: A new league projection points toward an unprecedented financial jump that could trigger another era of massive deals.
articles.body:
The NHL's Board of Governors gathered this week for their latest round of meetings, but the number that reportedly turned the most heads had nothing to do with current rosters or this season's standings race.

According to Elliotte Friedman, the league shared its initial projection for the 2028-29 salary cap, and the figure is staggering: $127.5 million (U.S.). If that estimate holds, it would represent a $14 million leap from the prior season, making it the single largest year-over-year increase in the entire salary cap era.

To put the trajectory in perspective, this season's cap sits at $104 million. Next year it climbs to $113.5 million under the second year of a three-season agreement between the NHL and NHLPA that has already pushed the ceiling to record territory.

The engine behind the surge is revenue. Commissioner Gary Bettman reportedly indicated that revenue projections for the upcoming season sit at roughly $8.1 billion in mixed currency. That kind of growth naturally feeds into the cap formula and explains why the league's long-range estimate is so aggressive.

For players, the news is a windfall. This past summer already saw contracts reach new heights, with deals for Leo Carlsson, Macklin Celebrini, and Cale Makar pushing into previously uncharted financial territory. A cap north of $125 million would only accelerate that trend, giving teams substantially more room to build rosters and reward top talent.

Not everyone stands to benefit equally, though. Smaller-market Canadian franchises that earn the bulk of their revenue in Canadian dollars could face a difficult squeeze. A cap denominated in U.S. currency climbing this fast puts pressure on organizations whose income does not rise at the same pace.

It is worth noting that the $127.5 million figure is an estimate, not a locked-in number. Revenue can fluctuate, and the final cap is calculated using a formula tied to actual hockey-related revenue. Projections shared at Board of Governors meetings have shifted before.

The league appears to be entering a new financial chapter entirely. How teams, agents, and players adapt to a cap that could jump $14 million in a single offseason will be one of the defining storylines heading into the second half of the decade.

articles.title: International break curse strikes Arsenal again as Havertz is set for scan
articles.summary: Arsenal were victims of the international break injury curse for much of last season, with Martin Odegaard particularly affected during the campaign’s first...
articles.body:
Arsenal were victims of the international break injury curse for much of last season, with Martin Odegaard particularly affected during the campaign's first international window.

The Gunners dreaded those breaks that forced them to release their players for international duty, and they have once again become victims. The latest concern involves Kai Havertz , who was forced off during the first half of Germany's match against the Netherlands last night.

Havertz suffers injury during international duty

The window has only just begun, and Havertz has already suffered an injury after pulling up during Germany's match. The Germans consider him one of their most important players, while the attacker has been working hard to remain valuable to his national team.

Havertz wants to stake a claim for a place in the team under Jurgen Klopp, and he started the match against the Netherlands. However, his injury before half-time will be a major concern for Arsenal, particularly given his importance to their attack.

The extent of the damage remains unknown, and Havertz was not the only German player to suffer an injury during the match. Jamal Musiala was also forced to leave the pitch after picking up an injury.

After the fixture, Klopp said via Standard Sport :

"They're probably out for us, but I hope they'll be back soon (for their clubs)."

The comments indicate that further assessment will be required before the extent of Havertz's injury becomes clear. Arsenal will therefore have to wait for the results of his scans before knowing how long he could be unavailable.

Havertz has been in excellent form since the start of the season and has been starting ahead of Viktor Gyokeres . His injury could therefore represent a significant blow to Arsenal, particularly if he is ruled out for an extended period.

The Gunners will now hope that the scans provide positive news and that Havertz can return to action for Arsenal as soon as possible.

articles.title: Red Wings’ Simon Edvinsson Contract Plan Reportedly Revealed
articles.summary: The Red Wings reportedly prefer a bridge contract for Simon Edvinsson, a decision that could preserve cap flexibility but create future risk.
articles.body:
The Detroit Red Wings may be leaning toward a bridge contract with Simon Edvinsson instead of immediately committing to a long-term extension.

The Winged Wheel Podcast reported Friday that this is Detroit's preference, attributing the information to Elliotte Friedman. No agreement has been announced, and neither the Red Wings nor Edvinsson's camp has publicly confirmed the reported structure.

Edvinsson is one of Detroit's most important pieces on the blue line. The 23-year-old was among the NHL's notable restricted free agents this offseason after recording nine goals and 25 points in 72 games last season, according to NHL.com .

Interim general manager Shawn Horcoff has already made it clear that getting Edvinsson signed is a priority. The emerging question is not whether Detroit values the defenseman. It is whether the club wants to pay for his prime years now or wait for another season or two of evidence before making that larger commitment.

A Bridge Deal Would Give Detroit Short-Term Flexibility

A bridge deal usually gives a young player a shorter contract at a lower cap hit than a long-term extension. For Detroit, that could preserve flexibility while the organization continues to work through major roster and leadership questions.

The Red Wings have been direct about their urgency to get Edvinsson under contract, with Horcoff saying the club hoped to have something completed soon. Detroit's focus on a new Edvinsson deal has not changed.

A shorter deal would also allow Detroit to better assess Edvinsson's next stage of development. He has already become a trusted NHL defenseman, but the organization could be betting that a bridge contract keeps today's cap number more manageable while it determines how high his offensive ceiling and all-around role can climb.

Detroit Would Also Be Accepting Future Risk

The tradeoff is clear. If Edvinsson continues ascending, his next contract could become considerably more expensive.

A long-term deal carries more immediate risk because Detroit would be committing major money before seeing the full finished version of the player. A bridge agreement shifts more of that risk to the club's next negotiation, when Edvinsson may have an even stronger case for a major raise.

That is why the reported preference matters. It suggests Detroit may want certainty on the player's current value before making a long-term bet, even though it believes he is a core piece moving forward.

With Shawn Horcoff serving as interim GM , the final contract structure could reveal plenty about how the Red Wings want to manage their roster during this front-office transition.

articles.title: Eric Nicksick: Sean Strickland sparred with road rash day after accident
articles.summary: UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland is a gym rat.
articles.body:
UFC middleweight champion Sean Strickland is a gym rat.

On Monday, Strickland got into a motor vehicle accident while sitting in the passenger seat of a UTV with no helmet on. The accident left Strickland with scratch marks all over his head, where he said the vehicle "rolled like six times."

However, that didn't deter Strickland (31-7 MMA, 18-7 UFC), who showed up to the gym the next day according to his head coach Eric Nicksick.

"He was at sparring yesterday," Nicksick told MMA Junkie Radio. "What am I going to do? Just send the guy home? He comes rolling in with a road rash all over him, and I'm like, 'So, how did that go last night?' And he was like, 'Yeah, it was pretty rough.' And I was like, 'What are you doing here?' And he goes, 'We've got to spar.' All right, put your sh*t on. Let's go. Dude's a monster, bro. We're a bunch of cowboys and outlaws in that gym."

This isn't the first time Strickland was involved in a motor vehicle accident. In 2018, Strickland had a serious motorcycle accident which hospitalized him and left him out of action for two years.

Strickland hasn't competed since dethroning Khamzat Chimaev in an upset title win at UFC 328 in May. He is expected to make his first title defense against Nassourdine Imavov.
